A slope field for a differential equation is shown at the points with integer coordinates.

options.why: The first term depends on the starting index; check the term for the first value of n.

The formula is $$\frac{a}{1 - r}$$, not $$\frac{a}{1 + r}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x + y$$ with $$f(1) = 4$$. Using the tangent line at $$x = 1$$, what is the approximation of $$f(1.1)$$?

questions.stem: Which of the following is an equation of the line tangent to the graph of $$f(x) = x^{2} - 5x - 1$$ at $$x = -3$$?

options.why: This swaps the x- and y-coordinates of the point of tangency.
This slope drops the derivative of $$-5x$$.
This uses the function value $$23$$ as the slope.
Correct. The point is $$(-3, 23)$$ and the slope is $$f'(-3) = -11$$.

questions.stem: Let $$W(t)$$ be the amount of water in a tank, in gallons, at time t hours. Which of the following is the best interpretation of $$W'(4) = -3$$?

options.text: The amount of water at time $$t = 4$$ hours is -3.
options.why: This describes $$W(4)$$, the value of the function, not its rate of change.

options.text: The average rate of change of the amount of water over the first 4 hours is -3 gallons per hour.
options.why: The derivative is an instantaneous rate at one input, not an average over an interval.

options.text: The amount of water is decreasing at a rate of 3 gallons per hour at time $$t = 4$$ hours.
options.why: Correct. A derivative at a point is an instantaneous rate of change, with units of output per unit of input.

options.text: The amount of water changes by -3 over the first 4 hours.
options.why: This describes a total change over an interval, which is an integral of the rate, not the derivative at one point.

questions.explanation: $$W'(4)$$ is the instantaneous rate of change of $$W$$ at time $$t = 4$$ hours. Its sign (negative) says the amount of water is decreasing, and its units are gallons per hour.

questions.stem: The functions $$f$$, $$g$$, and $$h$$ satisfy $$g(x) \leq f(x) \leq h(x)$$ for all $$x$$, where $$g(x) = -3 - x^2$$ and $$h(x) = -3 + x^2$$. What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$$?

options.why: This is the input value being approached, not the output.
Correct. Both $$g$$ and $$h$$ approach $$-3$$ as $$x \to 0$$, so the Squeeze Theorem forces $$f$$ to approach $$-3$$ too.

options.text: It cannot be determined without a formula for $$f$$.
options.why: The Squeeze Theorem determines the limit without a formula for $$f$$, because the bounds share the same limit.
This adds the limits of $$g$$ and $$h$$; the squeeze gives their common value.

questions.explanation: $$\lim_{x \to 0} g(x) = -3$$ and $$\lim_{x \to 0} h(x) = -3$$. Since $$f$$ is trapped between them, the Squeeze Theorem gives $$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = -3$$.

questions.stem: If $$\int_0^{1} f(x)\,dx = -4$$ and $$\int_0^{5} f(x)\,dx = -3$$, what is $$\int_{1}^{5} \left(-3f(x) + 5\right)dx$$?

options.why: This forgets to multiply the integral of $$f$$ by $$-3$$.
This adds the two given integrals; the integral from a to b is their difference.
The integral of the constant $$5$$ over an interval of length $$4$$ is $$20$$, not $$5$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int_{1}^{5} f(x)\,dx = \int_0^{5} f - \int_0^{1} f = 1$$. By linearity, the requested integral is $$-3 \cdot 1 + 5 \cdot 4 = 17$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives the length of the curve $$y = e^{2x}$$ from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 1$$?

options.why: The derivative must be squared.
The integrand needs a square root and a squared derivative.
Correct. Arc length integrates $$\sqrt{1 + [f'(x)]^2}$$.
This squares the function instead of its derivative.

questions.explanation: For $$y = f(x)$$, $$L = \int_a^b \sqrt{1 + [f'(x)]^2}\,dx$$, and here $$f'(x) = 2e^{2x}$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{\pi/6} \sin(6x)\,dx$$?

options.why: This forgets the factor $$\frac{1}{6}$$ from the inner function.
The antiderivative of $$\sin u$$ is $$-\cos u$$; this drops the negative sign.

questions.explanation: $$\int \sin(6x)\,dx = -\frac{1}{6}\cos(6x) + C$$. Evaluating: $$-\frac{1}{6}\left[\cos\pi - \cos 0\right] = \frac{2}{6}$$.

questions.stem: A twice-differentiable function $$f$$ satisfies $$f'(2) = 0$$ and $$f''(2) = 4$$. Which of the following must be true?

options.text: $$f$$ has a point of inflection at $$x = 2$$.
options.why: f″ is not zero, so this is not a candidate for inflection.

options.why: The second derivative test applies because f″ ≠ 0.
A maximum needs f″ < 0.

questions.explanation: By the Second Derivative Test, $$f'(c) = 0$$ with $$f''(c) > 0$$ gives a relative minimum.

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = \frac{8}{3}t$$ and $$y'(t) = \frac{5}{3}t^2$$. What is the speed of the particle at $$t = 3$$?

options.why: Speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector, not the sum of its components.
This is the slope of the path, not the speed.
This forgets the square root.

questions.explanation: At $$t = 3$$, $$\vec{v} = \langle 8, 15 \rangle$$, so the speed is $$\sqrt{64 + 225} = 17$$.

questions.stem:
Which of the following series converge?

I. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^n}{\sqrt{n}}$$

II. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2}$$

III. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^2 + 1}$$

options.why: Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II converges, III diverges.
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II converges, III diverges.
Correct. I: converges (alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values). II: converges (p-series with p = 2 > 1). III: diverges (limit comparison with the harmonic series).
Check each series with an appropriate test: I converges, II converges, III diverges.

questions.explanation: Series I converges: alternating series test, but p = 1/2 for the absolute values. Series II converges: p-series with p = 2 > 1. Series III diverges: limit comparison with the harmonic series.

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = x^{3} - 12x + 1$$ on the closed interval $$[-3, 5]$$?

options.why: This is a candidate value, but not the largest one. Check every critical point and both endpoints.
This is the absolute minimum value.
This is a candidate value, but not the largest one. Check every critical point and both endpoints.
Correct. Compare $$f$$ at the critical points $$x = \pm 2$$ and the endpoints: the largest value is $$66$$.

questions.stem: If $$f(x) = \arcsin\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$, what is $$f'(1)$$?

options.why: Correct. $$f'(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2/4}} \cdot \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4 - x^2}}$$.
This applies the inner factor twice.
This leaves out the inner derivative $$\frac{1}{2}$$.

questions.explanation: $$\frac{d}{dx}\arcsin u = \frac{u'}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}}$$. With $$u = \frac{x}{2}$$, $$f'(1) = \frac{1/2}{\sqrt{3/4}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$$.

questions.stem: Let $$y = f(x)$$ be the solution to $$\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2 - y$$ passing through the point $$(-2, 2)$$. What is $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at that point?

options.why: Sign error: the derivative of −y is −dy/dx.
This differentiates x² but treats y as a constant; y depends on x.
Correct. $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2x - \frac{dy}{dx}$$, and $$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2$$ at the point.
This is dy/dx, the first derivative.

questions.explanation: Differentiate implicitly: $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = 2x - \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - (x^2 - y)$$. At $$(-2, 2)$$: $$-4 - 2 = -6$$.

questions.stem: The sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^{3}}$$ is approximated by its first 9 terms. What is the smallest upper bound on the error given by the alternating series error bound?

options.why: The exponent stays the same as in the series.
This is the last term used, not the first one omitted.
This skips a term: the bound is the very next term.
Correct. The error is at most the first omitted term.

questions.explanation: The terms alternate, decrease in size and approach 0, so $$|S - S_{9}| \leq b_{10} = \frac{1}{10^{3}}$$.

questions.stem: What is $$\lim_{x \to 0} \frac{\sqrt{x + 36} - 6}{x}$$?

options.why: Substitution gives $$\frac{0}{0}$$, an indeterminate form.
Correct. Rationalizing gives $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 36} + 6}$$, which approaches $$\frac{1}{12}$$.
The expression is undefined at 0, but rationalizing shows the outputs approach a single number.
This forgets that the conjugate denominator is $$\sqrt{x + 36} + 6$$, which approaches $$12$$, not $$6$$.

questions.explanation: Multiply by $$\frac{\sqrt{x + 36} + 6}{\sqrt{x + 36} + 6}$$. The numerator becomes $$x$$, which cancels, leaving $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 36} + 6} \to \frac{1}{12}$$.

questions.stem: Which of the following gives the area of the region enclosed by the polar curve $$r = 2 + \cos\theta$$?

options.why: Since $$r > 0$$ for every angle, the curve is traced once over $$[0, 2\pi]$$, not $$[0, \pi]$$.
This leaves out the factor $$\frac{1}{2}$$.
The radius must be squared.
Correct. Polar area is half the integral of $$r^2$$ over one full trace.

questions.explanation: $$A = \frac{1}{2}\int_\alpha^\beta r^2\,d\theta$$. Because $$2 > 1$$, $$r > 0$$ for all $$\theta$$ and the curve closes after $$2\pi$$.

questions.stem: A function $$f$$ has $$f(2) = -1$$, $$f'(2) = 5$$ and $$f''(2) = 4$$. Using the second-degree Taylor polynomial for $$f$$ about $$x = 2$$, what is the approximation of $$f(2.1)$$?

options.why: The quadratic term must use $$(x - a)^2$$, not $$(x - a)$$.
This forgets to divide the second derivative by $$2!$$.
This is the tangent-line (first-degree) approximation.

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line tangent to the curve $$x^2 + y^2 = 169$$ at the point $$(12, 5)$$?

options.why: This is y/x. The tangent line is perpendicular to the radius, whose slope is y/x, so the tangent slope is −x/y.

This is −y/x, which inverts the correct ratio.

questions.explanation: Differentiate implicitly: $$2x + 2y\,y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x}{y}$$. At $$(12, 5)$$ this is $$-\frac{12}{5}$$.

questions.stem: An open-top box is made from a 12-inch by 12-inch square of cardboard by cutting equal squares of side $$x$$ from each corner and folding up the sides. What value of $$x$$ gives the box its maximum volume?

options.why: This is not a critical point of the volume.
This is not a critical point of the volume.
At this cut the base has zero width, which gives volume 0 (a minimum).

questions.explanation: $$V'(x) = (12 - 2x)^2 - 4x(12 - 2x) = (12 - 2x)(12 - 6x)$$. On $$0 < x < 6$$, the only critical point is $$x = 2$$, where $$V'$$ changes from positive to negative.

questions.stem: What is the coefficient of $$x^{3}$$ in the Maclaurin series for $$f(x) = \sin(3x)$$?

options.why: The constant must be raised to the same power as x.
Correct. Substitute into the known Maclaurin series.

questions.explanation: Factor the denominator as $$(x - 4)(x + 1)$$. Solve $$x - 14 = A(x + 1) + B(x - 4)$$: substituting $$x = 4$$ and $$x = -1$$ gives $$A = -2$$ and $$B = 3$$. Each piece integrates to a logarithm.

questions.stem: What is the interval of convergence of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(x - 2)^n}{n\cdot 5^n}$$?

options.why: The radius is 5, from the factor $$5^n$$.
The endpoints are reversed: the right endpoint gives the divergent harmonic series.
The left endpoint gives $$\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$$, which converges.
Correct. Ratio test gives $$|x - 2| < 5$$; the left endpoint gives an alternating harmonic series (converges), the right endpoint the harmonic series (diverges).

questions.explanation: Ratio: $$\left|\frac{(x - 2)^{n+1}}{(n + 1)5^{n+1}}\cdot\frac{n\,5^n}{(x - 2)^n}\right| \to \frac{|x - 2|}{5}$$, so $$|x - 2| < 5$$. At $$x = 7$$: $$\sum \frac{1}{n}$$ diverges. At $$x = -3$$: $$\sum \frac{(-1)^n}{n}$$ converges.

questions.stem: What is $$\int_0^{\infty} e^{-2x}\,dx$$?

options.why: Sign error: the integrand is positive, so the integral is positive.
The antiderivative of $$e^{-kx}$$ has a factor $$\frac{1}{k}$$, not $$k$$.
The exponential decays fast enough for the area to be finite.
Correct. $$\lim_{b \to \infty}\left[-\frac{1}{2}e^{-2x}\right]_0^b = \frac{1}{2}$$.

questions.explanation: $$\int_0^b e^{-2x}dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - e^{-2b}\right) \to \frac{1}{2}$$.

questions.stem: A 5-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall. The bottom of the ladder slides away from the wall at a constant rate of 4 feet per second. How fast is the top of the ladder moving, in feet per second, when the bottom is 3 feet from the wall?

options.why: This swaps the roles of x and y.
The two ends do not move at the same speed; their rates depend on the position.
The top slides down, so its rate is negative.
Correct. $$x^2 + y^2 = 25$$ gives $$x\frac{dx}{dt} + y\frac{dy}{dt} = 0$$. With $$x = 3$$, $$y = 4$$, $$\frac{dy}{dt} = -\frac{3(4)}{4}$$.

questions.explanation: Let $$x$$ be the distance from the wall and $$y$$ the height. $$2x x' + 2y y' = 0$$, so $$y' = -\frac{x x'}{y} = -\frac{3 \cdot 4}{4} = -3$$ feet per second (the top is moving down).

questions.stem: What is the slope of the line tangent to the polar curve $$r = 2 - 3\cos\theta$$ at $$\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$$?

options.why: This is $$\frac{dr}{d\theta}$$, which is not the slope.
Correct. $$\frac{dy}{d\theta} = 3$$ and $$\frac{dx}{d\theta} = -2$$.
This is $$\frac{dx/d\theta}{dy/d\theta}$$, upside down.
Sign error in $$\frac{dx}{d\theta} = r'\cos\theta - r\sin\theta$$.

questions.explanation: With $$x = r\cos\theta$$ and $$y = r\sin\theta$$: at $$\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$$, $$r = 2$$ and $$r' = 3$$. So $$\frac{dy}{d\theta} = r'\sin\theta + r\cos\theta = 3$$ and $$\frac{dx}{d\theta} = r'\cos\theta - r\sin\theta = -2$$; the slope is $$-\frac{3}{2}$$.

questions.stem: Using a left Riemann sum with the four subintervals indicated by the table, what is the approximation of $$\int_0^{10} R(t)\,dt$$?

options.why: This is the right Riemann sum.
Correct. Multiply each subinterval's width by the appropriate height and add.

questions.explanation: The widths are 2, 1, 4, 3. Use the left endpoint of each subinterval, multiply by the width and add: $$114$$ gallons.

questions.stem: What is the sum of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} 7\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)^n$$?

options.why: This divides by $$r$$ instead of $$1 - r$$.

questions.stem: The temperature of a room, in degrees Fahrenheit, is modeled by $$H(t) = 80 + 15\sin\left(\frac{t}{8}\right)e^{-t/20}$$, where $$t$$ is measured in hours. What is the instantaneous rate of change of the temperature at $$t = 12$$, in degrees Fahrenheit per hour?

options.why: This is the average rate of change over $$0 \leq t \leq 12$$, not the instantaneous rate.
This is the temperature itself, not its rate of change.
This multiplies the rate by the time, which is not a rate.
Correct. The calculator's numerical derivative of $$H$$ at $$t = 12$$ gives -0.338; the temperature is decreasing.

questions.stem: The sum of $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n^{2}}$$ is approximated by its first 8 terms. What is the smallest upper bound on the error given by the alternating series error bound?

questions.stem: What is the area of the region enclosed by the graphs of $$y = 3\cos\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)$$ and $$y = x^2 - 1$$?

questions.stem: Sand is added to a pile at a rate modeled by $$R(t) = 25 + 4\sin\left(\frac{t}{4}\right)\sqrt{t + 1}$$ cubic feet per hour, for $$0 \leq t \leq 5$$. At time $$t = 0$$ the pile contains 78 cubic feet of sand. How much sand is in the pile at $$t = 5$$?

options.why: This adds the rate at one instant, not the accumulated amount.
This assumes the rate stays at R(T) for the whole time.
Correct. $$78 + \int_0^{5} R(t)\,dt$$.

questions.explanation: Amount = initial amount + accumulated change = $$78 + \int_0^{5} R(t)\,dt \approx 78 + 147.305 = 225.305$$ cubic feet.

questions.stem: What is the area of the region bounded by the polar curve $$r = 2 + 1.5\sin^2\theta + \frac{\cos 3\theta}{2}$$ and the rays $$\theta = 0$$ and $$\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$$?

questions.stem: A particle moves in the plane with $$x'(t) = 2\cos\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right)$$ and $$y'(t) = e^{t/3}$$. What is the total distance the particle travels from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 3$$?

questions.stem: What is the absolute maximum value of $$f(x) = xe^{-x/4} + \frac{\sin x}{4}$$ on the interval $$[0, 11]$$?

questions.stem: What is the radius of convergence of $$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{n\,(x + 1)^n}{6^n}$$?

options.why: The center is not the radius.
The series converges for all x only when the ratio limit is 0 for every x.
Correct. The ratio test gives $$\frac{|x + 1|}{6} < 1$$.
